title: British registered designs: diamond marks (1842-1883) and Rd numbers (1884-1991)
applies_to: The diamond-shaped registration mark and the "Rd" or "Rd No" number on British ceramics, glass, metalwork and other goods. Either dates the registration of the design or shape, so the piece was made then or later, often years later. It does not name the maker.

sources.name: The National Archives, Discovery catalogue: Board of Trade design representations and registers, BT 50 (designs 1-518643, 1884-1908), BT 52 (non-textile representations from 1908) and BT 53 (non-textile registers, 1908-1991)
The National Archives research guide, 'Registered designs 1839-1991': diamond marks (section 7), appendices 1 and 2 (month and year codes)
Geoffrey A. Godden, Encyclopaedia of British Pottery and Porcelain Marks (London, 1964), pp. 526-528: the diamond key and Rd numbers registered each January, 1884-1909
J. P. Cushion and W. B. Honey, Handbook of Pottery and Porcelain Marks (London, 1956), Appendix A: the diamond key

caveats: A registration dates the design, not the piece: a pattern or shape could stay in production for decades. The date is the earliest the piece can be.
The registrant was often, not always, the maker: retailers, designers and foreign firms registered designs too.

Godden marks his January numbers from 1902 on as approximate. The Archives' books show them running early: no. 420000 was registered in October 1903, not January 1904, and no. 550000 in September to November 1909.
From 1910 to the late 1940s the Archives catalogue its picture books by year only; the registers narrow most numbers to a few months.
Textile designs had their own numbers after 1908; these are the non-textile numbers that appear on ceramics, glass and metalwork.
Australia, New Zealand and other countries also printed "Regd" numbers; a number with no British context may not be British.

layout.1842-1867: class number at the top in a circle; the year letter in the top corner under it; the month letter in the left corner; the day number in the right corner; the parcel number in the bottom corner
layout.1868-1883: class number at the top in a circle; the day number in the top corner under it; the parcel number in the left corner; the year letter in the right corner; the month letter in the bottom corner

quirks: R was used for the month 1-19 September 1857 (Godden, the Archives, Cushion & Honey)
K was used for the month in December 1860 (Godden, the Archives, Cushion & Honey)
From 1 to 6 March 1878 G was used for the month and W for the year, in place of W and D (the Archives, Cushion & Honey; Godden gives W for the year)
Godden also reads O as January (C or O); the Archives and Cushion & Honey give C only
